title: Advanced Process Substitution knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Advanced Process Substitution”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Comparing output streams” under lesson 144, “Advanced Process Substitution”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Advanced Process Substitution”?
options: Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Document the minimum Bash version and use complex features only when their behavior is tested.
questions.answer_key: Document the minimum Bash version and use complex features only when their behavior is tested.
questions.explanation: Document the minimum Bash version and use complex features only when their behavior is tested. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Advanced Process Substitution”?
options: Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Track task lifecycles, define cleanup on normal exit and interruption, and collect each status.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
questions.answer_key: Track task lifecycles, define cleanup on normal exit and interruption, and collect each status.
questions.explanation: Track task lifecycles, define cleanup on normal exit and interruption, and collect each status. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
